title: 1. Meaning of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)

blocks.content:
Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines given to the State to establish a just and welfare-oriented society.
They aim to promote social and economic democracy in the country.
Although they are fundamental in the governance of the country, they are not enforceable by courts.

items: DPSPs aim to establish social and economic democracy rather than mere political democracy.
Despite being non-enforceable, DPSPs are explicitly fundamental in the governance of the nation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) act as guidelines for the State to establish a just and welfare-oriented society.
The primary goal of DPSP is to promote social and economic democracy.
DPSPs are fundamental to the governance of the country.
DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced in a court of law.
